status_note: Still open on main (a4d8e00342d0, = v0.108.0): [`functions_arithmetic.yaml` L982-L1046](https://github.com/substrait-io/substrait/blob/a4d8e00342d0/extensions/functions_arithmetic.yaml#L982-L1046) define the shifts by description only, with no option and nothing on a count outside `[0, width)` or bits shifted out of `shift_left`. The test cases allow a negative base (`shift_left.test` L9-L12: `shift_left(-3::i64, 1::i32) = -6::i64`). No existing issue; options in general: [#254](https://github.com/substrait-io/substrait/issues/254).
summary: `shift_left` and `shift_right` (`functions_arithmetic.yaml`) do not say what a shift count below 0 or at least the base's width gives, nor whether `shift_left` may shift bits out. They have no option for it. A negative base is allowed by the test cases (`shift_left(-3::i64, 1::i32) = -6::i64`).
repro: `shift_left(1::i64, 64)`, `shift_right(-5::i64, 64)`, `shift_left(-1::i64, 1)`, `shift_left(2^62::i64, 2)`: the YAML's descriptions define none of them.
DuckDB 2.0: `1 << 64` raises, `-1 << 1` raises, `(2^62) << 2` raises (a bit shifted out), `-5 >> 64` is `0`.
handling: The core allows each engine's recorded behaviour (raise, `0`, drop the bits) as the option `shift_range` (docs/core-semantics.md, D3). The reference drops the bits shifted out and raises for a count outside `[0, 63]`; DuckDB's written plan guards both shifts.
Could be expressed as: An option such as `on_shift_overflow: [ERROR, ZERO, WRAP]` for the count, and the existing `overflow` for bits shifted out of `shift_left`.
